transcript: This intimate theatre piece is performed in a real life planetarium tucked away in the Lower East Side Girls Club. The show is called 73 Seconds, written and performed by Jared Mezzocchi, and it tells the story of his mother, a school teacher who once worked at NASA and was a candidate for a historically significant space mission. But now, as she begins to lose her memory, Jared finds himself in the position of having to pass along her incredible story himself. So we see him wrestle with a mix of pride and frustration, not only as he yearns to know more about her time at NASA, but also other moments throughout his life when his mother felt like a mystery to him. Of course, the idea to perform it in a real planetarium ties into themes of space travel, but also education and sort of the mysteries of the universe. Of course, they do make use of the domed ceiling at various points, sometimes with sort of makeshift projections, but other times with the actual planetarium projector. For the sake of the novelty, I kind of wish they had used the full functionality of the projector more than they did, but I don't think the piece needed it otherwise. It's pretty clear why he wanted to turn this into a theatre piece, because this NASA story is quite remarkable and specific to her, while the way he frames it has a more broadly relatable emotional resonance. I will say everything he included in the show, I understood why he included it, but the actual knitting together of these stories into a script sometimes felt a little awkward. But even if it didn't totally live up to its potential, it was still a story worth telling and fun to see it in this setting.
